name: Ampicillin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Ampicillin is excreted largely unchanged in urine. The US injection label gives no kidney dose adjustment and no dialysis dosing; its overdose section says ampicillin-class antibiotics are removed by hemodialysis but not by peritoneal dialysis. Dosing in kidney impairment needs specialist input.
kidney_function_basis: Label gives no kidney measure or bands.

bands.recommendation: Usual dose (label gives no kidney adjustment).
The label gives no kidney dose adjustment. Ampicillin is excreted largely unchanged in urine, so levels rise as kidney function falls. Specialist input.

hd: Ampicillin-class antibiotics are removed by hemodialysis (label overdose section); no dose is given. Time doses after the session. Specialist input.
pd: Not removed by peritoneal dialysis (label overdose section); no dose is given. Specialist input.
crrt: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) gives no regimen for this drug. Specialist input.
dialyzable: Hemodialysis: yes. Peritoneal dialysis: no (label overdose section, for ampicillin-class antibiotics). About 20% protein bound.
monitoring: Kidney function; neurologic toxicity at high doses with kidney impairment; rash; diarrhea (CDAD).

pediatric.usual_dose: Under 40 kg: respiratory and soft tissue 25 to 50 mg/kg/day divided every 6 to 8 hours; gastrointestinal and genitourinary 50 mg/kg/day divided every 6 to 8 hours; bacterial meningitis 150 to 200 mg/kg/day divided every 3 to 4 hours (label).
pediatric.neonates: 28 days or younger, meningitis and septicemia (label Table 1): gestational age 34 weeks or less and postnatal age 7 days or less, 100 mg/kg/day every 12 hours; 34 weeks or less and 8 to under 28 days, 150 mg/kg/day every 12 hours; over 34 weeks, 150 mg/kg/day every 8 hours.
